niche_preference_profile: This user most often prefers interfaces with strong visual hierarchy, clear grouping, and obvious primary actions. They repeatedly favor rounded cards/buttons, spacious layouts with breathing room, and polished modern styling. Their color preference is mixed by context, but they consistently like higher contrast, decisive accent usage, and cohesive palettes. They often prefer modular card-based structures over long uninterrupted pages or split fragmented layouts, and they respond well to screens that feel focused, scannable, and intentionally organized.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers clear sectioning, strong headline/price/action emphasis, readable grouping, and layouts that make the main message or task immediately obvious.
Prefers more padding, whitespace, open spacing, and less cramped compositions, unless the denser option clearly improves task efficiency or information access.
Prefers softer rounded cards, buttons, pills, and modal containers over sharper rectangular or edge-to-edge treatments.
Usually prefers simplified, less cluttered information presentation, but will favor denser layouts when they surface more actionable controls, comparisons, or planning details in a task-focused way.
Prefers content organized into unified cards, modular blocks, contained panels, or centered modal overlays rather than long text pages, fragmented sections, or flat list rows.
Prefers cohesive palettes with stronger contrast, vivid accents, and clearly highlighted active or primary elements rather than muted, low-contrast, or mixed-emphasis color treatments.
Prefers clearly visible, emphasized CTAs and action controls that are integrated near the main content or task, rather than hidden, weak, or overly separated actions.
